::: {.about-lead}
# About me

I am **Felix Akwasi Sarpong**, a Ghanaian mathematician and statistician pursuing graduate study at **Georgia State University** in Atlanta. My academic path has moved from mathematics and statistics into scientific computing, machine learning, optimization, and computational research.
:::

## Academic path

My training includes undergraduate study at **Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST)**, graduate mathematical-sciences training at **AIMS Ghana**, and graduate work in the Department of Mathematics and Statistics at **Georgia State University**.

At AIMS Ghana, my research included machine learning for time-series causality. That work contributed to research on **resting-state effective brain connectivity using reservoir computing**, connecting mathematical modeling, machine learning, and computational neuroscience.

At Georgia State, my graduate work has included statistical learning, Bayesian data analysis, survival analysis, computational optimization, biostatistics, experimental design, and pattern recognition.

## Research interests

- Statistical and scientific computing
- Machine learning and pattern recognition
- Numerical optimization and numerical linear algebra
- Bayesian computation and Monte Carlo methods
- Survival and longitudinal data analysis
- Time-series causality and computational neuroscience
- High-dimensional predictive modeling

## Technical toolkit

**Languages:** R, Python, MATLAB, SQL, SAS, C  
**Scientific workflow:** RStudio, Quarto, LaTeX, Git/GitHub, Jupyter, Linux  
**Methods:** regression, regularization, simulation, optimization, Bayesian inference, resampling, survival analysis, longitudinal models, machine learning

## Beyond computation

I value teaching, clear technical communication, reproducible research, and building tools that make quantitative ideas easier to understand and use.
